idiom_name: generic container View with a @ViewBuilder content closure; container owns state, call site supplies the views
implementation_notes: SwiftUI realizes the pattern directly: a container view is generic over its content and takes it as a @ViewBuilder closure, documented as 'a custom parameter attribute that constructs views from closures', so the call site decides what is rendered - including multi-statement content with conditionals - while the container owns state and interaction and the framework re-renders on state change. What replaces the classic wrapper/subclass structure is the generic Content: View parameter plus @State/@Binding: the container exposes behaviour through the binding it hands the closure, not through markup it dictates. The imperative form (a UIView subclass with a delegate) is only justified where SwiftUI is not in use.
pitfalls: The container is generic over Content, so the closure's type is fixed at the call site; erasing to AnyView to vary content costs diffing performance.
@State is tied to view identity: a container re-created in a ForEach/sheet/list gets fresh state, so state that must survive re-parenting has to be lifted or passed as a Binding.
ViewBuilder closures compile into builder calls (buildBlock/buildEither), which restricts statements inside them - imperative 'let'/'if let' plumbing belongs outside the closure.
A stored closure property makes every new closure a changed value; extract expensive content or make it Equatable to avoid re-render churn.
